config.title: min(), max(), clamp()

intro.title: min(), max(), clamp()
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll learn how to use CSS's min(), max(), and clamp() functions to create flexible and responsive designs. You'll build a simple webpage with elements that adjust their size based on screen width, using these functions to set minimum, maximum, and clamped values for properties like width and font-size. The core concept is using mathematical functions directly in CSS to create dynamic layouts without complex media queries. You'll work with CSS properties and function syntax to make your designs more adaptable to different devices. By the end, you'll understand how to implement these functions to control element dimensions and spacing responsively.
intro.usecase: The min(), max(), and clamp() functions are essential for creating responsive designs that work across different screen sizes. In real-world applications, you'll use clamp() to create fluid typography that scales smoothly between minimum and maximum font sizes on marketing websites. Dashboard interfaces use min() to ensure sidebar panels never exceed a readable width on large monitors, while max() prevents form inputs from becoming too narrow on mobile devices. These functions help developers build components like navigation menus, data tables, and modal dialogs that adapt intelligently to various viewports without complex media queries.

objectives: Implement the min() function to create responsive width constraints
Apply the max() function to establish minimum size boundaries
Construct fluid typography using the clamp() function
Configure spacing values that adapt between defined limits
Manipulate container dimensions with combined min() and max() functions
Integrate clamp() into padding declarations for adaptive layouts
Initialize responsive design patterns using these CSS math functions

font-size: clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 2rem);
